root_cause.text: In `drivers/crypto/ccp/sev-dev.c`'s `sev_ioctl_do_pdh_export()`, the SEV PDH export path copied `pdh_blob`/`cert_chain` to userspace using firmware-returned lengths even when the PSP command had failed, so an invalid-length error could cause `copy_to_user()` to read past the kernel-allocated buffers.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (ret || WARN_ON_ONCE(argp->error)) goto e_free_cert;` immediately before the `copy_to_user()` calls, and the CVE/commit message explicitly states that on firmware failure due to too-small user buffer/length, “copying the number of bytes firmware requires will overflow the kernel-allocated buffer and leak data to userspace,” with KASAN reporting a slab-out-of-bounds in `sev_ioctl_do_pdh_export`.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch adds `if (ret || WARN_ON_ONCE(argp->error)) goto e_free_cert;` immediately before the `copy_to_user()` calls, and the CVE/commit message explicitly states that on firmware failure due to too-small user buffer/length, “copying the number of bytes firmware requires will overflow the kernel-allocated buffer and leak data to userspace,” with KASAN reporting a slab-out-of-bounds in `sev_ioctl_do_pdh_export`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Clarify in comments that firmware-provided certificate blob lengths are always returned to user space, whether they represent required or actual written sizes.
intent_record.what: The single-line comment above the assignments to input.cert_chain_len and input.pdh_cert_len was replaced with a multi-line comment explaining that firmware returns the blob lengths, either the minimum required length or the actual length written, and that these lengths are returned to user space.
intent_record.how: This change does not alter runtime behavior; the code still copies data.cert_chain_len and data.pdh_cert_len into the user-visible input structure, but the updated comment clarifies the meaning of those values in both query-length and actual-write cases.

intent_record.intent_summary: Abort PDH export and clean up if the command failed or returned an unexpected error before copying certificate data to userspace.
intent_record.what: A new conditional check was added after the preceding operation in sev_ioctl_do_pdh_export(): if ret is non-zero or WARN_ON_ONCE(argp->error) evaluates true, execution jumps to the e_free_cert cleanup label before attempting the copy_to_user() of the PDH certificate blob.
intent_record.how: This prevents the function from proceeding to copy certificate data to userspace when the earlier operation failed or when the firmware-reported error field is unexpectedly set, ensuring cleanup happens immediately and avoiding use of invalid or incomplete export results.

grouping_result.intent: Clarify in comments that firmware-provided certificate blob lengths are always returned to user space, whether they represent required or actual written sizes.
Abort PDH export and clean up if the command failed or returned an unexpected error before copying certificate data to userspace.

relevance_review.reason: The change concerns the same PDH export certificate-length handling that caused the bug: firmware-returned blob lengths are returned to userspace even on error. Although it is a comment clarification, it directly documents the behavior at the root of the vulnerability.

The change directly addresses the root cause by stopping the PDH export path and cleaning up when the PSP command fails or returns an unexpected error, preventing copy_to_user() from using invalid firmware-returned lengths on kernel buffers.

candidates.rationale: This is the unsafe userspace copy in the PDH export path. Per the root cause, it uses the firmware-returned length even when the PSP command failed, enabling an over-read from the kernel buffer.
This assigns the firmware-returned PDH certificate length into the value later used for copy_to_user(), even on error paths, which can make the copy size invalid.
This stores the firmware-returned certificate-chain length for later userspace copying without ensuring the command succeeded, contributing to the invalid-length over-read condition.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the userspace copy operation in sev_ioctl_do_pdh_export(). The vulnerability root cause states that PDH export copied pdh_blob/cert_chain to userspace using firmware-returned lengths even when the PSP command had failed, allowing copy_to_user() to read past the kernel-allocated buffers.

This propagates the firmware-returned certificate-chain length into the userspace-visible/output length state even when the PSP command may have failed. That unchecked length is part of the condition that enabled the later unsafe userspace copy with an invalid size.

This assigns the firmware-returned PDH certificate length without requiring successful command completion. That invalid or oversized length could then be used by the subsequent copy_to_user() path, causing an over-read from the kernel buffer.

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function body for sev_ioctl_do_pdh_export() is sufficient because it includes the allocation checks, command path, and the final copy_to_user() operations that are relevant to the root cause. The vulnerability condition is present: after firmware processing, the function copies data back to userspace using user-controlled/firmware-updated lengths without any visible check that the PSP command succeeded before using those lengths. In the snippet, the copies are unconditional on command success: `if (pdh_blob) { if (copy_to_user(input_pdh_cert_address, pdh_blob, input.pdh_cert_len)) ... }` and `if (cert_blob) { if (copy_to_user(input_cert_chain_address, cert_blob, input.cert_chain_len)) ... }`. The root cause says failed PSP commands could still leave invalid lengths that then drive copy_to_user() past the allocated buffers. This commit only changes `__user` pointer handling by introducing `input_pdh_cert_address` and `input_cert_chain_address`; it does not add any guard such as checking the PSP command return/result before copying, nor does it validate the returned lengths against allocated buffer sizes after the command. Therefore the vulnerable construct is still present, and the fix is not present.

The vulnerable construct is present: after `ret = __sev_do_cmd_locked(SEV_CMD_PDH_CERT_EXPORT, &data, &argp->error);`, the code unconditionally copies firmware-returned lengths back into `input` via `input.cert_chain_len = data.cert_chain_len;` and `input.pdh_cert_len = data.pdh_cert_len;`. It then proceeds to `copy_to_user(input_pdh_cert_address, pdh_blob, input.pdh_cert_len)` and `copy_to_user(input_cert_chain_address, cert_blob, input.cert_chain_len)` without checking whether `ret` indicates the PSP command failed.
